course.title_zh: 看懂 xABCDE 创伤初评

modes.purpose: For clinicians who need a concise xABCDE route and key observation points.
For residents, junior clinicians, and students who need staged explanation.
For staged information release, clinical judgement, and reassessment practice.

objectives: Distinguish observation, reporting, team action, and reassessment.
Use xABCDE as a shared trauma reasoning language rather than a bedside algorithm.
Recognize when new information should send the team back to an earlier stage.
Explain why missing visible bleeding or airway deterioration can distort priorities.
audience: medical students in supervised trauma education

stages.title: Catastrophic external bleeding
stages.question: Which visible bleeding concern must be reported before deeper survey work continues?
stages.summary: Learners scan for visible bleeding cues, report location and change, and preserve team workspace.
stages.clinical_significance: Visible bleeding can alter initial priority and team resource allocation.
stages.key_action: Report observed facts to the team; senior clinicians and local policy determine treatment.
stages.common_mistake: Treating x as a checkbox rather than an active first look and repeat look.

stages.guideline_source: ACS ATLS 11 public source index; NICE NG39 public page

stages.title: Airway and c-spine protection
stages.question: Can the patient maintain airway protection while the team preserves cervical spine precautions?
stages.summary: Learners observe speech, airway sounds, face or neck cues, and c-spine protection status.
stages.clinical_significance: Airway risk and neurologic change may interact with breathing and circulation priorities.
stages.key_action: Report airway risk cues and confirm senior-team awareness; no independent airway instruction is provided.
stages.common_mistake: Jumping to a device or procedure before reporting what is actually observed.
